sentences.text: Rocasaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived in South America.
Its skeleton is highly pneumatic, meaning it contains many air-filled spaces similar to its close relatives Neuquensaurus and Saltasaurus.
This animal is considered one of the titanosaurians with the highest degree of postcranial pneumatization, including the tail, sacral vertebrae, and possibly the pelvic girdle.
Despite being a sauropod, Rocasaurus was relatively small, measuring 8 meters in length, 3 meters in height, and weighing 4 tonnes.
Evidence suggests that Rocasaurus died and was rapidly buried by sediment, leading to good preservation of articulated skeletons.
Rocasaurus was discovered in Argentina in 2000 within the Allen Formation, dating to the middle Campanian to early Maastrichtian (75 to 70 million years ago).
Fossils were collected between 1989 and 1994 from Salitral Moreno, located 25 km south of General Roca in Río Negro Province, Argentina.
Leonardo Salgado and Claudia Azpilicueta formally described the species Rocasaurus muniozi in 2000.
The genus name refers to the discovery near General Roca, while the species name honors Juan Carlos Muñoz for his support of paleontological research.
The holotype MPCA-Pv 46 was found in the lower Allen Formation dating to the Campanian-Maastrichtian and consists of a juvenile skullless skeleton.
The holotype includes two cervical vertebrae, three dorsal vertebrae, two sacral vertebrae, two mid-caudal vertebrae, both ilia, a left pubis, both ischia, and a left femur.

Rocasaurus differs from other saltasaurines by having a wide ventral fossa divided by a thin longitudinal septum in anterior tail vertebrae, and by ilium and ischium morphology with notably developed ischial blades.
The strongly procoelous tail vertebrae feature large lenticular pneumatic pores directed horizontally on the sides, with an oval-shaped inferior channel connected to the spongy interior bone.
Later researchers noted that sacral vertebrae are extremely pneumatic, even more so than in other titanosaurs, and that the limbs appear quite elongated, unlike the stout legs of Saltasaurus.
Studies of Rocasaurus tail vertebrae revealed extensive internal pneumatization with small cavities separated by bone trabeculae.
Researchers identified possible pneumatic bone tissue (pneumosteum) in only two tail vertebrae, suggesting it is not a universal marker for air sac invasion in sauropods.
Rocasaurus lived in a diverse ecosystem that included turtles, fish, crocodiles, birds, ornithopods, abelisaurids, and megaraptorial theropods.
Rocasaurus appears to be closely related to saltasaurid dinosaurs such as Saltasaurus and Neuquensaurus.
Rocasaurus is classified within the subfamily Saltasaurinae.
Rocasaurus was classified within the subfamily Saltasaurinae in the year 2000.
Rocasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically from 75 to 70 million years ago.
Rocasaurus lived in what is now northern Patagonia, Argentina, during the Late Cretaceous (approximately 75 to 70 million years ago).
Rocasaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
Fossils of Rocasaurus have been found in the Allen Formation in northwestern Patagonia, specifically in the provinces of Río Negro and Neuquén.
Saltasaurians like Rocasaurus are found in the northwestern region of Argentina, specifically in the Allen Formation of Río Negro and Neuquén provinces.
It is likely that saltasaurians like Rocasaurus originated after the fragmentation of Gondwana and the opening of the South Atlantic Ocean during the mid-Cretaceous.
Recent research suggests there may be a sauropod taxon in the Allen Formation distinct from Rocasaurus, though this is currently only possible evidence.
